prompt:
Compare speed and velocity by answering the following:
(a) State one similarity between speed and velocity. [1]
(b) State the main difference between speed and velocity. [1]
(c) An aircraft flies along a horizontal circular arc at a constant speed of 180 m s^-1. Explain why its velocity is not constant even though its speed does not change. [1]

answer.text:
(a) Both describe how fast an object moves / both have the same magnitude and SI unit (m s^-1).
(b) Speed is a scalar quantity (magnitude only), whereas velocity is a vector quantity (magnitude and direction).
(c) Because the aircraft moves in a curved path, its direction of motion is continuously changing; since velocity includes direction, the velocity changes.

mark_scheme: Part (a) [1 mark]: Both have the same SI unit (m s^-1) / both quantify rate of motion / have magnitude.
Part (b) [1 mark]: Speed is scalar / magnitude only, whereas velocity is vector / has magnitude and direction.
Part (c) [1 mark]: The direction of motion is changing (so velocity changes).
hints: Consider units and physical meaning for the similarity.
Think about what vector means for an object following a curve.
solution:
(a) Both share the same SI unit, m s^-1, and quantify rate of motion.
(b) Speed is a scalar (magnitude only), whereas velocity is a vector (magnitude and direction).
(c) The aircraft's direction of motion changes continuously along the arc, so its velocity changes.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Part (a): state shared unit m s^-1 or rate of motion (1 mark).
Step 2: Part (b): state scalar vs vector / direction requirement (1 mark).
Step 3: Part (c): link circular motion to changing direction and changing velocity (1 mark).
